purpose: Reviewed public-source supplements for exact-version technical review. These records strengthen reviewer evidence and may be incorporated into lesson content only through normal versioned content/review workflows.
integrityBoundary: A supplemental source mapping is not a scientific/editorial approval and does not modify a published lesson. Lesson content changes must increment the lesson version and obtain renewed exact-version review.

reviewUse: Verify that pesticide-label information access and early-entry instruction remain distinct from ordinary worker authorization.
Verify the distinction between application-time exclusion controls and post-application restricted-entry intervals.
Verify hierarchy-of-controls language for respiratory/allergic exposure prevention and that PPE is not framed as the sole control.
Verify that cannabis-production occupational-asthma risk is presented as a documented occupational-health concern without diagnosing individual learners or workers.
Verify that quarantine/hold controls are not conflated with pesticide application-time exclusion or REI controls.
Verify escalation language when treated-area status, labeling information, or worker authorization is incomplete.
Use as an integrated cross-check for chemical/PPE, treated-area, exposure-control, symptom-reporting, and authority-boundary scenarios.
Do not convert source availability into handler/applicator authorization or medical diagnosis.
Cross-check that irrigation-water quality is taught as a measured input with laboratory/context dependence rather than as a single universal number.
Verify that pH, alkalinity, EC/salts and source-water context are distinguished.
Verify the distinction between pH and alkalinity and avoid presenting a generic greenhouse range as a universal cannabis target.
Confirm that meter/lab context and trend interpretation remain part of the decision.
Cross-check EC as an aggregate dissolved-ion/salt signal whose meaning depends on water, fertilizer, medium, method and crop context.
Avoid transferring extension threshold examples into fixed cannabis setpoints.
Verify that soil/soilless media differ in buffering, aeration, water retention and testing method.
Confirm that media-specific analytical methods are not mixed without noting method dependence.
Cross-check clean propagation-media and contamination-risk concepts.
Keep greenhouse propagation guidance separate from cultivar-specific cannabis propagation recipes.
Verify rooting-media and acclimatization instruction includes contamination/biosecurity context.
Use extension guidance for general protected-crop practice, not as a substitute for validated facility clone SOPs.
Cross-check IPM as prevention, scouting/monitoring, decision thresholds and integrated tactics rather than automatic pesticide use.
Keep pest-specific thresholds crop- and program-specific.
Verify representative scouting, plant-inspection, trap and recordkeeping principles.
Confirm that observation and mapping precede unsupported causal diagnosis.
Cross-check sanitation, incoming-stock/tool/water pathways, moisture/condensation, separation and transition controls.
Keep actual disinfectants, contact times and treatment choices controlled by validated facility procedures and labels.
Use hemp extension evidence only for general prompt-drying, humidity/airflow and mold/spoilage risk concepts.
Do not convert industrial-hemp drying guidance into a universal cannabis finished-product specification.
Cross-check storage discussion for moisture/heat/spoilage awareness while preserving product-specific QA requirements.
Treat facility specifications, validated packaging controls and jurisdictional requirements as controlling.
Cross-check that sensor placement is tied to the environment actually experienced by the crop and that atypical shade/location bias is considered.
Verify sensor maintenance, leveling/cleanliness and recalibration are treated as data-quality controls rather than assuming every reading is valid.
Verify PPFD is presented as photon flux density reaching a surface/canopy rather than watts or human-perceived brightness.
Cross-check measurement geometry, sensor placement and distance/context without copying non-cannabis crop intensity targets.
Verify DLI is presented as accumulated photosynthetic light over the day and distinguished from a single instantaneous PPFD reading.
Use extension material for measurement concepts only; cannabis-specific DLI targets require cannabis-specific evidence and facility validation.
Cross-check multi-factor differential reasoning against cannabis-specific evidence showing that nutrient symptoms and tissue measurements do not always align one-to-one.
Verify that infectious-disease possibilities, root-zone/nutrition factors and environmental context remain separate hypotheses until evidence supports a cause.
Verify that confirmation relies on appropriate next tests, repeated observations or laboratory/analytical evidence rather than visual symptom matching alone.
Keep diagnosis, treatment authority and escalation/reporting boundaries distinct.
Cross-check fertigation/root-zone troubleshooting as an integrated interpretation of solution, water, medium/root-zone, plant and historical data rather than symptom-only diagnosis.
Avoid turning research or extension examples into universal cannabis pH, EC or nutrient setpoints.
Verify standardized, representative scouting and recordkeeping as the basis for comparing pest/disease observations over time.
Keep crop- or facility-specific thresholds separate from general IPM monitoring principles.
Cross-check containment and prevention language against cannabis greenhouse disease-management evidence emphasizing clean stock, sanitation, irrigation/environment management and monitoring.
Do not imply independent pesticide selection/application authority; labels, registrations, facility SOPs and applicable law remain controlling.
Verify that propagation underperformance differentials include stock-plant health, pathogen pressure, sanitation, rooting-media/environment and process variation.
Keep corrective action evidence-bounded and controlled by validated propagation SOPs.
Cross-check deviation fact collection and process-timeline reconstruction against known postharvest variables including drying conditions, moisture/water activity, handling and storage.
Do not assume a single universal drying endpoint; distinguish observed facts from suspected cause.
Verify that drying trend interpretation considers temperature, humidity, moisture/water-activity behavior, time and spatial/process variation together.
Preserve facility-validated specifications and current QA requirements instead of treating literature examples as universal finished-product limits.
Cross-check morphology-based developmental and reproductive-stage observations against cannabis-specific peer-reviewed morphology evidence.
Keep visible morphology, developmental timing and causal interpretation separate so a recorded structure is not over-interpreted as proof of a genetic or environmental cause.
Cross-check integrated room inspection against cannabis-specific workplace hazard categories and the need to preserve safe authority boundaries during measurement work.
Verify irrigation and water observations remain measurement- and context-based rather than converting generic protected-crop examples into universal cannabis setpoints.
Cross-check representative sensor placement, measurement geometry and environmental context before interpreting trends or controller behavior.
Verify calibration, placement and measurement quality are treated as prerequisites to decisions rather than assuming every sensor reading is representative.
Cross-check supervisor-ready handoff against established human-factors principles of preparation, two-way communication, written plus verbal transfer and incoming-worker cross-checking.
Use HSE guidance as a transferable communication model only; facility procedures and U.S. jurisdiction-specific requirements remain controlling.
Cross-check integrated triage so nutrient/root-zone, plant-health/pathogen and process/postharvest explanations remain competing evidence-based hypotheses until discriminating evidence is available.
Verify the learner preserves uncertainty, conflicting evidence and next-test logic instead of reducing a multi-system case to visual symptom matching.
